hypotheses.claim: After recurrence/readout adaptation, the frozen encoder initializes latent coordinates poorly; recalibrating it may reduce initial and slow current errors.
hypotheses.test: Factor A: fit-only encoder recalibration with frozen decoder/recurrence, then freeze encoder for common training. No additional online inputs, dimensions or physical gates.
hypotheses.falsifier: If encoded-state errors fail to improve, or later regressions remain despite repaired initialization, this is not a sufficient explanation.

hypotheses.claim: Short truncated gradients favor local current improvements over longer recovery dynamics.
hypotheses.test: Factor B:128vs512tick BPTT, same512tick forward windows, data, initialweights and update budget. Report time/memory separately; retain nested checkpoints.
hypotheses.falsifier: If longer gradients do not improve slow development trajectories or eligible checkpoints, the observed gradient rotation alone did not identify a useful repair.

hypotheses.claim: Shared trunk and multi-channel family updates trade one current against another, especially within Na andCa families.
hypotheses.test: Shared gradient diagnostics: per-family norm andcosines, and initial/readout/rollout residuals. Do not change shared-trunk learning andBPTT together without a separate contrast.
hypotheses.falsifier: Consistently aligned gradients and no relation between conflict and regressions weaken this explanation.
